discovery: The X-ray free-electron laser based on self-amplified spontaneous emission (SASE)

nominees.name: Claudio Pellegrini
nominees.affiliation: University of California, Los Angeles and SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory, USA

nominees.name: Kwang-Je Kim
nominees.affiliation: Argonne National Laboratory and University of Chicago, USA

nominees.name: Jörg Rossbach
nominees.affiliation: University of Hamburg and DESY, Germany

subfield: Accelerator physics / X-ray optics and photon science
motivation: Pellegrini proposed, and Kim developed the theory of, the high-gain self-amplified spontaneous emission free-electron laser, showing that a relativistic electron beam in a long undulator could produce coherent, femtosecond X-ray pulses a billion times brighter than any synchrotron. Rossbach led the TESLA Test Facility/FLASH effort that first demonstrated SASE saturation at short wavelengths, the experimental proof that paved the way to LCLS, SACLA, European XFEL, SwissFEL and PAL-XFEL. These sources created a new kind of light: they allow single-shot imaging of biomolecules, femtosecond studies of chemical bonds forming and breaking, matter under extreme conditions, and nonlinear X-ray spectroscopy. As an X-ray spectroscopist I see daily how this invention has transformed the measurement of electronic structure and dynamics across physics, chemistry and materials science. It is a fundamental instrument invention with community-wide impact, in the tradition of the laser itself.
